A.explanation: This is $\text{kg m s}^{-2}$, which is the newton, the unit of force from $F = ma$.

B.explanation: This is force divided by time, $F/t$, which does not equal mass times velocity.

C.explanation: Force multiplied by time, $F \times t$, equals impulse which equals change in momentum, so $\text{N s}$ is a unit of momentum.

D.explanation: This is $\text{kg s m}^{-1}$, with velocity upside down, so it cannot equal $mv$ in $\text{kg m s}^{-1}$.

hints: Notice momentum is defined by $p = mv$, so start from $\text{kg}$ for mass and $\text{m s}^{-1}$ for velocity.
Connect force to momentum using impulse: resultant force $F$ acting for time $t$ gives $Ft = \Delta p$.
Compare each option to $\text{kg m s}^{-1}$ by remembering $1 \text{ N} = 1 \text{ kg m s}^{-2}$ and checking what multiplying or dividing by $\text{s}$ gives.
walkthrough: Recall the definition of momentum: $p = mv$, so its base unit is mass unit times velocity unit, $\text{kg} \times \text{m s}^{-1} = \text{kg m s}^{-1}$.
Recall the impulse result: $Ft = \Delta p$, so the unit of force times the unit of time must also be a unit of momentum.
Expand the newton: $1 \text{ N} = 1 \text{ kg m s}^{-2}$ from $F = ma$.
Multiply by seconds: $1 \text{ N s} = 1 \text{ kg m s}^{-2} \times \text{s} = 1 \text{ kg m s}^{-1}$, which matches the momentum unit exactly.
Check the others: $\text{kg m s}^{-2}$ is force, $\text{N s}^{-1}$ is $\text{kg m s}^{-3}$, and $\text{kg s m}^{-1}$ has $\text{s}$ and $\text{m}$ the wrong way round.
Therefore only $\text{N s}$ is equivalent to $\text{kg m s}^{-1}$. This is option C
